rows.l: +        Return the FULL details of EVERY reservation that belongs to a user, in one call.
+        Use this when the user wants to modify or cancel a reservation but does NOT know
+        the reservation id, or when they describe the trip by route/city/date instead of
+        by id (e.g. "my flight from New York to Chicago"). This returns all of the user's
+        reservations at once so you can pick the correct one by matching its ``origin``,
+        ``destination``, ``flights``, dates, cabin, or passengers — instead of guessing an
+        id or calling ``get_reservation_details`` repeatedly. Match the route the user
+        described against each reservation's ``origin``/``destination`` (IATA codes) and
+        the per-segment origin/destination before acting; do NOT assume the first
+            User: "I want to change my New York (JFK) to Chicago (ORD) trip." You do not
+            have the id. Call list_reservations(user_id='omar_rossi_1241'); scan the
+            returned list for the reservation whose origin is 'JFK' and destination is
+            'ORD'; use THAT reservation_id for the change.
+            user_id: The user ID, such as 'sara_doe_496'.
+            A list of full Reservation objects (same shape as get_reservation_details),
+            one per reservation id in the user's profile.
+            ValueError: If the user is not found.
+        Compute the EXACT amount the user will be charged or refunded for a proposed cabin
+        and/or flight change on an existing reservation, WITHOUT changing anything.
+        Call this BEFORE update_reservation_flights whenever the user asks "how much will
+        this cost", "how much will I be refunded", or "what is the price difference" for a
+        cabin downgrade/upgrade or a flight change. It uses the SAME pricing rules as
+        update_reservation_flights, so the number it returns is exactly what that write
+        would charge or refund. Report ``amount_refunded`` (for a downgrade) or
+        ``amount_due`` (for an upgrade) to the user verbatim.
+        IMPORTANT — do NOT compute this yourself from search_direct_flight prices. The
+        refund/charge is based on the prices ALREADY PAID and stored on the reservation
+        (reservation.flights[*].price), not on the current market fare. This tool reads
+        those stored prices for you; hand-computing from search results gives the wrong
+            Reservation GV1N64 is currently 'business' with 3 passengers and paid fares
+            561 + 1339 per passenger. The user wants 'basic_economy' on the same two
+            amount_refunded=5244 (i.e. the user is refunded 5244). Tell the user 5244.
+            reservation_id: The reservation ID, such as 'ZFA04Y'.
+            cabin: The cabin class the reservation would have AFTER the change, one of
+            flights: The COMPLETE list of flight segments the reservation would have after
+                the change (include every segment, even unchanged ones), each as
+              - num_passengers: number of passengers on the reservation
+              - current_total_paid: total already paid for the current flights (all pax)
+              - new_total: total the new flights/cabin would cost (all pax)
+              - net_change: new_total - current_total_paid (negative means a refund)
+              - amount_due: positive dollars the user must pay (0 if it is a refund)
+              - amount_refunded: positive dollars the user is refunded (0 if a charge)
+              - summary: a human-readable one-line description of the charge/refund
+            ValueError: If the reservation is not found.
+            ValueError: If a new flight segment is not available on its date.
+        if all(isinstance(flight, dict) for flight in flights):
+        # New total: mirror update_reservation_flights pricing exactly.
+            # A segment keeps its old price only if flight_number, date AND cabin are all
+            # unchanged; a cabin change forces every segment to be re-priced at the live
+        old_total_per_pax = sum(rf.price for rf in reservation.flights)
+                f"The user must pay an additional ${net_change} "
+            summary = "No price change; nothing is charged or refunded."
Update the flight information of a reservation.
+        The charge or refund equals (new flight/cabin total) minus (the total ALREADY PAID
+        and stored on the reservation) times the number of passengers — it is NOT computed
+        from current market fares. If the user asks how much they will be charged or
+        refunded BEFORE you make the change, call get_reservation_price_change first and
+        report the number it returns; do not compute it yourself from search_direct_flight.
